summary: Oldest surviving lighthouse on the Great Lakes, a Queenston-stone tower of 1808 on Toronto's Centre Island, lit until the late 1950s. Grounds open, tower closed.

structures.note: Built to 16 m (52 ft) including the lantern; raised in 1832 to about 25 m (82 ft) to the vane

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. The building is occasionally opened for tours and for Doors Open Toronto.

events.note: Hexagonal stone tower completed in 1808 (Library); Gazette notice of 16 March 1808
Tower raised; sperm-oil lamp from 1832; overall height 82 ft to the vane (Library)
Lightning struck the tower; a steel lantern and lightning rod had been fitted in 1878
Revolving apparatus: fixed white changed to a white flash every 45 seconds
Wooden fog alarm building 1,150 ft south-west of the tower; discontinued 1905
Gibraltar Point fog alarm permanently discontinued after a fog alarm was established at East Gap
Department report: the light from the Gibraltar Point lighthouse was permanently discontinued on 30 June 1907. The reports on file do not say when it was relit.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens placed atop the tower in July 1915 (Lighthouse Friends)
Electrified in 1916 (Library); winter 1916-17 (Lighthouse Friends). The 1917 report describes a white revolving light.
Changed to a fixed light (Library); Lighthouse Friends says fixed green
Operation given to the Metropolitan Toronto parks department, 23 May 1958
Replaced by a nearby signal tower (Library); inactive officially since 1958 (Rowlett). Lighthouse Friends says 1959.
Restoration photographed by the Toronto Star in 1962 (Library's photo caption)

wrecks.outcome: Wrecked on the south shore of the peninsula; the Library says the skipper seems to have been confused by the light
Ran aground on a bar north of the point; the lamp ran out of oil that night; the owner, Freeman Bay, was awarded £100
Foundered in a gale while anchored under Gibraltar Point, waiting for the wind to ease before entering the harbour; six of her crew reached shore, six drowned

corrections.why: 1956 appears only in the record and the Wikipedia infobox. The Library says the light was replaced by a nearby signal tower in 1958, and Metro Parks took over on 23 May 1958. The Directory says inactive officially since 1958. Lighthouse Friends gives 1959.
Same date as the light.deactivated correction. Lighthouse Friends' 1959 is recorded in the event note.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says inactive and the Directory line reads Active (inactive officially since 1958). The Library says the light is no longer used for its original purpose, and the Directory states it was inactive officially from 1958. Read together: no longer an aid to navigation since 1958-59.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28 (page images read on archive.org). 1905 report printed p.151 (scan 164), Appendix 19 above Montreal: 'Durnan, George | Gibraltar Point Light and Fog Alarm | ,, 31, 1854 | 625 00' confirmed on the image, so the printed page is 151, not 164 as the earlier footnote said; the footnote now gives scan 164 and printed 151. 1907 report printed p.165 (scan 174): 'McSherry, Patrick | Gibraltar Point | May 2, 1905 | 400 00' confirmed on the image. The story does not state the 1905 appointment date (the cached OCR does not place it beside the name). Resolute (1908 report, casualties heading 'nine months ending March 31, 1907', Toronto Division, 22 Nov 1906) read in OCR; its printed page (155) was not checked on the image. 1909 report 'permanently discontinued' on 30 June 1907, 1906 East Gap fog alarm, and 1917 'white revolving' (p.33) are read in OCR; their page numbers were not checked on the image. Disagreements stated: completion 1808 (TPL, LF) vs first keeper from 1809 (LF keepers list only); deactivation 1958 (TPL, Directory) vs 1959 (LF); the 1907 discontinuance vs LF's July 1915 lens and the 1916-17 electrification; the 1832 wreck's keeper's delay; the 1893 jawbone (LF: George Durnan uncovered a jaw bone; TPL: the keeper of the time allegedly found parts of a skeleton). Not settled: when the light was relit after 30 June 1907 (no report read says); Blake Matthews is not in the corpus, so his 1912-1918 service rests on LF alone (LF also says he left 'the following year' after the 1916-17 electrification). Legend: LF (beer; refused to sell; overcharged; soldiers killed him) and TPL (refused more liquor; soldiers beat him to death) differ in detail; the story attributes each. The 1877 inspection height (62 ft, LF) and the Library's 82 ft to the vane after 1832 are both stated. Names: Hollaway (LF) and Holloway (TPL) are both given; Radelmuller (LF keepers list) and Rademuller (LF text) are spelled Radelmüller as TPL does. Living people: no keeper after 1918 is named. Deedee Dodds (caretaker 1958, public role) appears in the roster only, not in the story. John Durnan (nephew, 1958 CBC) is not named. Wikipedia is not cited or used. Access: the Directory says the site is open daily and the tower closed; LF says grounds open, tower closed; the story says grounds open, tower closed, and that the Library says the building occasionally opens for tours.
